section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
section_1.content: Define a Bernoulli trial as an experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (S) or Failure (F). Emphasize that probability p must remain constant.
section_1.example: Visual animation: A coin flip. Heads (p=0.5) vs Tails (1-p=0.5).

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Conditions (BINS)
section_2.content: Introduce the BINS acronym: Binary (two outcomes), Independent trials, Number of trials is fixed, Success probability is constant.
section_2.example: Animated checklist showing a squirrel gathering nuts: Is it a success if it finds one? Are the tries independent? Yes!

section_3.title: The Binomial Formula
section_3.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Explain that C(n, k) calculates the number of ways to arrange 'k' successes in 'n' attempts.
section_3.example: Visual tree diagram showing 3 flips of a coin, highlighting how many paths lead to exactly 2 Heads.

section_4.title: Application: The Robot Scout
section_4.content: Walk through a practical scenario. A robot scout has a 70% chance of successfully identifying a mineral. If it scans 5 sites, what is the probability it finds exactly 4?
section_4.example: Step-by-step calculation: n=5, k=4, p=0.7. Show the probability distribution curve shifting as we solve it.

section_5.title: Summary & Visualization
section_5.content: Reiterate that the distribution shape depends on 'n' and 'p'. Preview how this predicts real-world likelihoods.
section_5.example: An animated histogram morphing shape as 'p' changes from 0.1 to 0.5 to 0.9.

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Visualization", [
            "Distribution shape depends on n and p.", 
            "Changing p morphs the histogram shape.", 
            "Binomial distributions predict real-world likelihoods."
        ])
        
        # Data for binomial(n=5, p=0.1)
        from scipy.stats import binom
        n = 5
        p = 0.1
        probs = [binom.pmf(k, n, p) for k in range(n + 1)]
        
        # Creating bars
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=prob * 4, width=0.6, fill_opacity=0.7, color=BLUE)
            for prob in probs
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Label for Sum
        sum_label = Text("Sum = 1", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(sum_label, "F5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Create(bars), Write(sum_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Morphing p
        for new_p in [0.5, 0.9]:
            new_probs = [binom.pmf(k, n, new_p) for k in range(n + 1)]
            new_bars = VGroup(*[
                Rectangle(height=prob * 4, width=0.6, fill_opacity=0.7, color=BLUE)
                for prob in new_probs
            ]).arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
            self.place_in_area(new_bars, "B2", "E5")
            
            self.play(Transform(bars, new_bars))
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Highlight highest probability
        max_idx = np.argmax([binom.pmf(k, n, 0.9) for k in range(n + 1)])
        highlight = bars[max_idx].copy().set_color("#FFD700").set_stroke(width=2)
        self.play(Indicate(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

        ])
        
        # Data for binomial(n=5, p=0.1)
        from scipy.stats import binom
        n = 5
        p = 0.1

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Use BINS to identify a binomial experiment.",
            "Binary outcomes and Independent trials are essential.",
            "Number of trials is fixed and p is constant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Binomial Conditions (BINS)", lecture_lines)
        
        bins = VGroup(
            Text("B - Binary Outcomes", color=WHITE),
            Text("I - Independent Trials", color=WHITE),
            Text("N - Number of Trials Fixed", color=WHITE),
            Text("S - Success Probability Constant", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.7)
        
        self.place_at_grid(bins, 'B2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color('#00CED1'))
        self.play(FadeIn(bins[0]), FadeIn(bins[1]))
